A 10-minute timer that fires while dirty() spends all five ring slots on identical copies and evicts the before-replace snapshot - the one taken at the only moment that loses data - within an hour. deleteSnapshot raced captureSnapshot. Both are read-modify-write over one index record; concurrently they lose one another's changes, leaving a resurrected snapshot or an orphaned payload. All snapshot mutations and listSnapshots now run through one queue.

A malformed index entry made trimSnapshotIndex compute NaN. Summing an undefined byteSize yields NaN, NaN > MAX_SNAPSHOT_BYTES is false, and the 2 MB budget silently switched itself off while the unlabeled row stayed in the Recover list forever. The index is normalized on every read: fields are coerced, and rows without an id - which name no payload and no actionable row - are dropped. Each of the three has a test that fails when its fix is reverted, verified by probe.

evidence.rollback: Reverting the commit loses no user data.
